thread.title: Sony: A Game You Want To Play - Sony Corporation (NYSE:SNE)

author: Joseph Heglin
title: Sony: A Game You Want To Play - Sony Corporation (NYSE:SNE)
text:
Sony Is The Gaming Stock You Want To Play Sony Corporation ( SNE ) has transformed themselves into a leader in the gaming industry with their last two big hit consoles the Playstation 3 and Playstation 4. They continue to add growth to multiple other areas, and will more than likely announce the release of the long awaited Playstation 5 in the coming year. With this announcement will come the opportunity to profit off of the company's success. If trends continue the company should set record highs in the near future as they streamline their already successful business.
Sony has made numerous moves in the past few years that have helped set them apart from competitors. Acquiring new publishing groups in music, beating just about every analyst's projections in the movie industry, and cutting back on their laggards such as the mobile industry have all helped the company prosper. SNE appears extremely undervalued where they currently sit and could easily go on a very nice run if more potential catalysts and acquisitions can come along.
Multi-Industry Leader
Sony Corporation ( SNE ), headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, has done fantastic things so far this year. The improvements can be easily seen in the raw financials. They have increased revenue from 7.60 trillion Japanese Yen to 8.53 trillion JPY (Figure 2) . A 12% increase in revenue over a year is an incredible feat for a mature company like Sony. Earnings saw an increase from 73.3 billion JPY to 490.8 billion JPY , a 570% increase as well for Sony. These up ticks in numbers are not a fluke. Sony has made substantial changes over the past few years that have helped them to become a leader in gaming, movies, music, and technology.
(Figure 1) Sony's Turnaround By The Numbers
Gaming
In the gaming industry Sony has turned the Playstation into the premier gaming system, beating Microsoft's Xbox so badly that they even quit reporting Xbox sales numbers for some time since the release of the PS4 (Figure 2) . Nintendo ( OTCPK:NTDOY ) is Sony's other main competitor and they have struggled with their consoles ever since their biggest release of the decade the Wii. Sony's Playstation has truly taken off, and Sony took advantage adding a must have paid subscription to online gaming. Playstation only games , such as the recent hit Spiderman game that came out this past month, help the PS4 stand out from Xbox and make it a no brainer when buying a gaming console. The time has come for the next generation of gaming consoles to come around. The Playstation 5 is rumored to be announced as soon as early 2019. This next console could potentially bring huge gains for Sony. As gaming continues to grow with competitive college scholarships now being offered to players, this is an expanding industry with plenty of possibilities on the horizon.
(Figure 2) Sony Expands The Gap in Console Sales Vs. Competitors
Music
One of Sony's lesser known divisions is their music division . Sony owns some of the biggest record labels in the world, and they continue to grow. Well known labels such as Columbia, RCA, Epic, Arista Nashville, and more are all a part of the Sony Corporation parent company. With huge stars such as Calvin Harris, P!nk, Tim Mcgraw, and many others, Sony has no shortage of potential in music. Music streaming has been the biggest area of growth for them, with total revenues in the division up over +12% in the past year. They continue to expand their reign by recently finishing their acquisition of EMI Music Publishing, which has been over 5 years in the making. With celebrity names such as Queen, Drake, Kanye West, Sam Smith, and more, it looks as if Sony is establishing a near monopoly on the music business. With the recent movie on Queen, Bohemian Rhapsody, Sony has profited on this renewed popularity through their music streaming business. The company makes 43% of their music entertainment profits from streaming according to their most recent earnings, so movie releases that rejuvenate classic bands and bring in profits are a huge bonus to this division of the corporation, and can bring earnings growth in places they have never had before. Sony is now the world's largest music publisher, and will see profits from these acquisitions for years to come.
A complete list of Sony's record labels, executives, and countries with offices can be found here.
Entertainment
Sony Entertainment has posted phenomenal gains this year in both film and television. In film they have beaten performance expectations on just about every movie they have released this year. One of Sony's best performers in film is the Spiderman universe. Sony owns the rights to Marvel's Spiderman and has posted huge numbers with movies such as Spiderman: Homecoming, (Figure 3) which has brought in nearly $1 billion in the theatre and home market. Another spin-off in Sony's Marvel Universe is the recent release Venom , which could bring even bigger numbers than Spiderman: Homecoming. As long as Sony holds a stake in the Marvel Universe they will be able to continue to produce blockbuster movies that rake in massive profits.
(Figure 3) Sony Picture's Spiderman: Homecoming Was A Huge Hit For The Company
Another movie series that has outperformed for Sony is the Goosebumps series. These movies have done much better than the expected numbers and offer Sony new opportunities around the Halloween season. Jumanji posted notable above expected numbers for Sony this year as well.
Sony's broad range of television series continue to perform nicely for them as well, with names such as Shark Tank, Jeopardy, the Goldbergs, and more. The group has had no shortage in the TV area. Sony also owns a hit network station in India that does very well.
Electronics
Sony also has one of the broadest varieties of hit electronics ranging from top of the line TV's to both audio and video technology. Sony creates innovative tech in everything from 4K Televisions to Cell Phones . This is historically around their second highest performing division (Figure 4) .
(Figure 4) SNE Year Over Year Performance By Division
Source: Statista
Sony will be a leader in several industries for years to come, and is a model for all large businesses to follow. They have already integrated a smaller 0.53% dividend into their stock as further incentive for investors as well. With such a broad range of products SNE offers one of the safer investments in the high growth technology industry. With a safety net in the financial branch of the company, Sony looks to be a strong buy in any market.
Current Value Sony Corporation is currently trading at a fantastic price, and looks to be a bargain compared to competitors. I think a breakout is very possible if the stock can start trading higher volume. Volume has been down drastically since earnings and so has the stock's price. The stock, for the most part, has been trading below the average volume levels of 1.1 million shares per day. This is mainly do to fear in the market as volatility continues to rise and investors stray from the tech industry. Sony remains a safe bet in my opinion with unique backing in their large financial segment they offer a lower risk than other many other tech companies.
Sony currently trades at an EV/EBITDA of 5.0x , drastically lower than competitors Microsoft and Nintendo which trade at an EV/EBITDA of 17.5x and 19.4x respectively. With a P/E (Price/Earnings Ratio) of 10.6x Sony again trades significantly lower than those same two competitors who have a P/E of 25.3x ( OTCPK:NTDOY ) and 44.9x ( MSFT ). Based off these numbers alone Sony in theory has the potential to nearly triple in value to trade along with these similar companies! Although I do not think that will happen, it can be reasoned that Sony has a lot of potential to run at the current value. One of the reasons Sony trades so much cheaper then their peers is their mobile phone branch that brings in much slower growth than the other segments of the company. Sony trades with a P/E very similar to Verizon ( VZ ) and as the company announced in their most recent earnings that they are cutting this division by nearly 50% this could lead to higher growth and a P/E that aligns more with MSFT and OTCPK:NTDOY .
Looking at theses companies YTD charts it can be seen that they do trade fairly similar, aside from Nintendo having a significant drop in a lack luster summer earnings call (Figure 5) . Sony has continued to flat out defeat Nintendo and Microsoft in gaming.
SNE data by YCharts (Figure 5) Sony Has Room To Run Yet This Year
Despite having a breakout couple of years, Sony has remained for the most part under the radar with very little coverage. Of the 2 Wall Street Analysts (Credit Suisse and Bernstein) that covered the stock both placed strong buy ratings on Sony, giving the stock a 1.0 recommendation rating with a 1 being a strong buy and a 5 being a strong sell.
Some of the weakness in Sony's stock compared to Microsoft most likely comes from their underperforming mobile division. Sony's cell phones have had a hard time keeping up with Apple ( OTC:APPL ) and Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ). They recently addressed this problem in their most current conference call stating they are working to cut mobile operating costs by 50% by 2021. This is good news as the company has identified their biggest issue and is working to fix it as soon as possible. If all works out Sony will continue to cut losses allowing the company to maximize gains.
With an approximately - 11% decline in the NASDAQ and NYSE since October, tech has had a major pullback. Sony reported fantastic earnings and looks to be a better value buy, by the day. Going into the 2019 year Sony has undeniable potential to run while still offering a safer investment than many major technology companies.
Reasons For Mispricing
Some reasons why Sony is most likely underpriced is due to the foreign trade wars and recent decline in the tech sector. The company's growth has been vastly overlooked. Very little of their profits would be hurt by the trade war, with their location in Japan instead of China, although the stock continues to fall with other foreign tech stocks. Many tech stocks are falling in price because their cycles are coming to an end. Although, I believe Sony's cycle has only just begun with the next release of a console, and it's all the better for them that they may be able to get the chips that make up this console at a reduced price because of this.
How To Play Sony Corp. With the announcement of the PS5 expected in 2019 and several earnings beats on the year, it is a great time to buy into Sony ( SNE ). Gaming is the company's #1 division, and Sony has historically gone on +35% runs with the news of a release of a new console, doubling in 2013 from $9.69 to over $21 (Figure 6) with the announcement of the release of the PS4. Gaming is one of the fastest growing businesses in the world, and Sony is in the premier position to take advantage of the high growth.
(Figure 6) It Is Easy To See The Runs Sony Goes On After Announcing New Consoles
Analysts are overlooking Sony's potential for growth in the next year in my opinion. When the PS4 was announced in 2013, annual EPS (Earnings Per Share) grew an absolutely incredible amount from - $5.55 to $0.43 (Figure 7)! Sony's 2018 EPS was $3.42, a 546.1% increase from 2017, and the 2018 to 2019 fiscal year had very nice growth as well up to nearly $5. Now analysts are projecting a dip in the 2020 fiscal year EPS down form $4.80 to $4.35. With the Playstation 5 on the horizon this number, although still very nice, it seems a little low when looking at prior growth on new console release years. With growth in both music and film, and cutbacks on the slow growing mobile division, it would not be a surprise if Sony continued the trend and posted another incredible year of growth as they did in 2012-2013. Even if the company grew half as much as they did the last time they released a new console that would still place 2020 fiscal year estimates well above the conservative 4.35 mark analysts are currently placing on SNE.
SNE Normalized Diluted EPS (NYSE: TTM ) data by YCharts (Figure 7) EPS Growth Signals Sony Could Be Well Undervalued Going Into The Next Year
Revenue is projected to grow 1.20% as well next year. This looks low as well, as gaming has taken off over the past decade, and analysts do not seem to be giving Sony enough credit for being a leader in this charge.
Another area Sony could find growth is in Virtual Reality. Sony has only begun to integrate Playstation VR into games and could potentially reach a lot of new consumers if this idea catches on (Figure 8) . It will be interesting to see how VR plays out in the future for not just Sony, but all gaming oriented companies.
(Figure 8) Playstation VR Is Being Integrated Into More And More Playstation Games
A growing movie and music fan base is also very positive for Sony. They are firing on all cylinders and it is just a matter of time before we see a breakout. With more potential catalysts this stock could very well have record highs on the horizon. The company continues to seek out new acquisition opportunities with over $2 billion in free cash flow in their most recent quarter alone. Tech is going through a correction and this allows for a fantastic entry price on Sony into what could be an amazing year.
One reason investors tend to go towards Microsoft or Apple when looking to add tech to their portfolio is because of Sony's financial division. The theory here is that the financial segment Sony owns will slow growth down over time compared to these other high powered tech companies. I like the financial segment at Sony as it offers diversity to the company's portfolio that is not found in any of their competitors. Even if the market does turn bearish in the future, Sony offers a slightly less risky investment in my opinion with the backing of this low growth, risk lowering financial segment.
The financial segment, Sony Financial Holdings, is mainly involved in life insurance and banking (Figure 9). Their total assets have slowly grown year over year and their revenues continue to outperform competitors as well. Some of their customers include nurses and other businesses. The company has a fantastic philosophy stating , "The Sony Financial Group seeks to become the most highly trusted financial services group by customers. To this end, the Group will combine many different financial functions (savings, investment, borrowing, and protection) to provide high-value-added financial products and high-quality financial services that meet every customer's financial needs." The company will work to go above and beyond to keep their reputation in line and that is exactly what you want from a finance sector. Sony finance helps lower risk by diversifying their portfolio in more than just tech, and that is something you cannot get with companies like Nintendo ( OTCPK:NTDOY ). With raising of interest rates, financial groups have had a lot more volatility of late, so it will be interesting to see exactly how this sector performs for Sony going forward.
(Figure 9) Some Of The Areas Sony's Financial Segment Covers
Valuation
With the release of the PS5 eminent, the growth in their music entertainment booming, and the success they have had in the film industry I am placing a $65-78 price target on Sony over the period of the next 8-12 months. I came to this valuation as I believe the company is at least 10% undervalued by looking at low P/E, EV/EBITDA values, and performance against competitors, and then I think the stock could easily run another 15-30% with the growth a new console would bring in 2019 and past trends. This stock looks like a tremendous opportunity if you have the patience to wait out the undeniably good news that should come out in the next fiscal year. As long as the company continues to beat earnings expectations Sony is a great investment in tech.
With Revenue growth expected to be much higher than this last year, and EPS beats expected due to low analysts estimates the stock should have no trouble posting similar, if not much better growth than this past years 15% run.
Risks
With the market volatility on the rise technology can be a risky investment. I think Sony is a safe investment as long as their 50 day moving average does not cross the 200 day moving average which would form a "death cross" pattern. This could occur if the stock falls below approximately the $45 mark in the next month. If this were to occur momentum of the entire market would most likely be bearish and the risk would outweigh the reward in my opinion (Figure 10). If Sony does dip below this mark or if the market falls into a recession Sony will not be able to reach these proposed figures. The foreign trade wars and tariffs have not taken a huge hit on Sony as they have on many other foreign companies. Much of this is due to the fact that a lot of Sony's profits come from digital products such as music and digital gaming.
SNE data by YCharts (Figure 10) Sony's Moving Averages Are A Good Indicator On How Things Could Play Out
Going Forward
It is very unlikely the stock would reach this low point, so the reward far outweighs the risk in the case of Sony. The company is in a much better position to ride out the trade war then many other foreign companies thanks to their digital media. Sony is an undiscovered strong buy going into 2019, and has the potential to be a big hit for investors, as an ongoing turnaround has gone very well for SNE . With a growing dividend that acts as a cherry on top, Sony is a great play when looking to add tech to your portfolio.
Disclosure: I am/we are long SNE, MSFT, AAPL.
